title.narrative: Inclusive Services and Opportunities for Host Communities and Displaced Rohingya Population

description.narrative: The deveplment objective of the Bangladesh - Inclusive Services and Opportunities for Host Communities and Displaced Rohingya Population Project is to improve access to human capital services for vulnerable host communities and displaced Rohingya population. The project components consist of the following: Component 1: Building Community Resilience and Self-Reliance (US$30 million equivalent (credit); US$40 million equivalent (grant); Component 2: Supporting Education Opportunities for Children (US$40 million equivalent (credit); US$20 million equivalent (grant); Component 3: Enhancing Social Care and Economic Empowerment (US$25 million equivalent (credit); US$25 million equivalent (grant); Component 4: Healthier Communities (US$80 million equivalent (credit); US$55 million equivalent (grant); Component 5: GBV Response and Prevention (US$17.5 million equivalent (credit), US$17.5 million equivalent (grant); Component 6: Contingent Emergency Response (US$0 million).

title.narrative: Percent change in help seeking behavior for women and men participating in SASA activities.

comment.narrative: The indicator will capture change is help seeking behavior among SASA participants, defined as, using, or encouraging GBV uptake. Numerator will be number of men and women who report using or encouraging others to use GBV services. Denominator will be the number of men and women who report seeing/hearing GBV happening in the community in the past year.

title.narrative: Workdays generated by short-term work opportunities

comment.narrative: This indicator measures the cumulative number of workdays generated under (1) EGPP+ (HC), and (2) Rohingya community services/works program (DRP). Data is disaggregated by HC and DRP as well as by gender within each community sub-indicator. Progress is reported based on the updated semi-annual report submitted by WFP and information shared by DDM on EGPP+.

Visits to use psychosocial services and case management services for gender-based violence response and prevention

comment.narrative: The indicator measures number of visits by women and girls to use psychosocial services and case management services provided through One-stop Crisis Centers/Cells/union level health facilities among host and Women-Friendly Spaces/Women and Youth Support Centers among DRP. The case management services include safety plans and referral to legal, shelter, medical and livelihood services. Kindly note that, Progress - "Actual (Previous)" - was reported incorrectly in the last ISR, the correct figure for this would have been 175,000 (as of August 14, 2025), the team provided a cumulative estimate in the previous ISR.
